content.intro: Learn django with a separate frontend through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Django with a Separate Frontend matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines django with a separate frontend as part of localization, accessibility, and user experience. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Serving an API to a frontend application; Authentication considerations; CORS and CSRF boundaries; Environment configuration; Coordinating API and frontend deployments. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Serving an API to a frontend application
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

items.title: Authentication considerations
items.text: Authentication identifies a user; authorization determines what the user can do. Prefer Django’s built-in password/user/session machinery and test account recovery and anonymous access.

items.title: CORS and CSRF boundaries
items.text: CSRF protection verifies that a state-changing browser request is associated with a valid token. Keep middleware/template token use and safe-cookie/HTTPS configuration aligned; CSRF is not an authorization substitute.

items.title: Environment configuration
items.text: Configuration for Environment configuration should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

items.title: Coordinating API and frontend deployments
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
